QUEBEC-REPORTED TELEVISION BROADCASTS OF SEPARATIST PROPAGANDA
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, it is a very serious question that I should like to submit to the house. It concerns the Quebec T.V. station CFCM which rented weekly programs to separatist parties and also authorized adepts of the RIN and other movements such as the Phalange, to use its facilities to speak in abusive language.
Of course, I would not want this admonishment to be considered as a direct attack on a personal friend, Mr. Jean Pouliot, a very brilliant man, who is director of the Quebec division and also the son of Dr. Adrien Pouliot, one of the great pioneers of French broadcasting in western Canada.
However, a very serious problem arises. One party, namely the RIN, intends to run candidates at the next election and, for that reason, it proposes to use television to make its views known.
Section 10 of the Broadcasting Act stipulates that programs must be essentially Canadian. This means that all programs must be essentially Canadian. But American programs are allowed. There is nothing against so-called

Canadian programs. This section does not prohibit such programs over a fundamentally Canadian network. But it is exaggerated to allow anti-Canadian programs, programs that split the Canadian confederation, and I feel that this is a flagrant violation of section 10 of the Broadcasting Act.
Because we must avoid at any cost throwing our country into another political crisis when demagogues will have the opportunity to be heard as much as they want, to condemn confederation and try to destroy Canada.
Such a thing must be prevented. That is why I ask tonight the minister or his representative to be kind enough to call the attention of the board of broadcast governors to that problem, so that it will investigate, consider and listen to the recording of the speeches which were delivered in order to determine the extent to which the law was violated and what kind of sanctions can be imposed.
Mr. Speaker, I insist. Everywhere we hear talk of separatism. Mayor Jean Drapeau and the minister of natural resources of Quebec speak of two associated states; the St. Jean Baptiste societies condemn co-operative federalism. We wonder where we are going with all that.
We must avoid, at all cost, another phenomenon like Caouette, emerging in this country, because I even say I am sure that there are separatist members sitting in this house. We must prevent such a phenomenon, such an attack against confederation, and we must avoid such a political upheaval.

speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, the hon. member's argument is both childish and stupid.
I say we must prevent another upheaval and the appearance of another Caouette. We must prevent government instability and accuse separatists of openly flouting the law when they condemn confederation and call for its dissolution. We are threatened and that is what I want to prevent.
I would ask the minister or his representative to have an investigation carried out in connection with those programs and to ensure that the latter are no longer carried over the Canadian network. We have a right to insist on the application of section 10. We have a right to insist on a basically Canadian network.

speakerposition: Parliamentary Secretary to the Secretary of State of Canada
subtopic: QUEBEC-REPORTED TELEVISION BROADCASTS OF SEPARATIST PROPAGANDA
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, I should not like anybody to be misled by the interpretation of section 10 of the Broadcasting Act adopted inadvertently by the hon. member. That section does not refer to the political views enunciated by speakers on Canadian radio or Canadian television. Now that the hon. member for Lotbiniere (Mr. Choquette) has identified for the house the particular program and the particular station that has caused him distress, I can assure him that his comments will be drawn to the attention of the board of broadcast governors, which board has the right to review the log of a station to ascertain if its policy with respect to equal treatment for political and controversial views is being respected. I say this merely to reassure the hon. member, and not to imply in the slightest degree that the program in question, which I did not see, was unfortunate.
